content: 1. Polymyxin B sulfate should never be injected into the eye. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution must not be introduced directly into the anterior chamber of the eye or injected subconjunctivally. 2. Topical antibiotics, particularly neomycin sulfate, may cause cutaneous sensitization. The exact incidence of hypersensitivity reactions, such as skin rash, due to topical antibiotics is not known. 3. Sensitization to topical antibiotics typically manifests as itching, redness, and swelling of the conjunctiva and eyelid. In some cases, sensitization may present as a failure to heal. 4. During prolonged use of topical antibiotic products, patients should undergo periodic examinations for signs of sensitization. If such signs are observed, the patient should discontinue the product. Symptoms usually resolve quickly after stopping the medication. 5. Patients who experience sensitization should avoid using products containing the same ingredients in the future. 6. Prolonged use of NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution may lead to the overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms, including fungi. If superinfection occurs, appropriate measures should be taken. 7. Bacterial resistance to NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution may develop. If purulent discharge, inflammation, or pain worsens, the patient should stop using the medication and consult a physician. 8. There have been reports of bacterial keratitis associated with the use of topical ophthalmic products in multi-dose containers that were inadvertently contaminated by patients. This is more likely in individuals with concurrent corneal disease or disruption of the ocular epithelial surface. 9. Allergic cross-reactions may occur, potentially preventing the use of related antibiotics such as kanamycin, paromomycin, streptomycin, and possibly gentamicin for future infections. 10. Patients should be instructed to avoid allowing the tip of the dispensing container to touch the eye, eyelid, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination. 11. Sharing this product between individuals may spread infection. Improper handling of ocular products can lead to contamination with bacteria that cause eye infections, potentially resulting in serious eye damage and vision loss. 12. If the condition persists or worsens, or if a rash or other allergic reaction develops, the patient should stop using the product and consult a physician. 13. Patients allergic to any of the listed ingredients should not use this product. The container should be kept tightly closed when not in use and stored out of reach of children. 14. Long-term studies in animals to evaluate the carcinogenic or mutagenic potential of polymyxin B sulfate or gramicidin have not been conducted. Neomycin has been shown to increase the frequency of chromosome aberrations in cultured human lymphocytes at high concentrations, but its effects on carcinogenesis and mutagenesis in humans are unknown. 15. Polymyxin B has been reported to impair equine sperm motility, but its effects on male or female fertility in humans are unknown. 16. NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted with neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B sulfate, or gramicidin. It is not known whether this product can cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity. It should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. 17. It is not known whether this drug is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when administering NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution to nursing women. 18. The safety and effectiveness of this product in pediatric patients have not been established. 19. Clinical studies of NEOSPORIN Ophthalmic Solution did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger patients. However, other clinical experience has not identified differences in responses between elderly and younger patients.
